### Changed
- **One OTLP collector for the whole platform: `global.observability.traces.otlp` (`endpoint`, `protocol`, the new `tenant`, `headers`) sets every exporter's destination** (giantswarm/giantswarm#36711). The meta chart writes it into each component key that is now `auto` by default: `kagent.otel.{tracing,logging}.exporter.otlp.endpoint` and `.tracing.exporter.otlp.protocol`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` in `kagent.controller.env` and `kagent.harness.env`, `muster.muster.observability.otel.{endpoint,protocol,headers}`, `klausGateway.observability.{otlpEndpoint,otlpHeaders}`, `substrate.otel.endpoint`, the tenant label in `substrate.podLabels` and `gateway.parameters.podLabels`, and the two OTLP entries of `gateway.parameters.dataPlaneEnv` (in both charts). A component key set to anything else wins. The defaults are the kube-system `otlp-gateway` on 4317 over gRPC with the `giantswarm` tenant, so every component renders as before. The tenant goes out as `X-Scope-OrgID` from kagent, muster and klaus-gateway, and as the `observability.giantswarm.io/tenant` pod label on Substrate and the data plane. `kagent.otel.{tracing,logging}.exporter.otlp.insecure` is `auto` too, `false` for an `https://` endpoint. An empty endpoint exports nothing and turns kagent's `auto` exporters and Substrate's signals off; an `X-Scope-OrgID` in `headers` that differs from `tenant` fails the render, and so does `protocol: http/protobuf` while klaus-gateway, Substrate or kagent's log exporter (gRPC only) would take the endpoint. The connectivity chart's OTLP egress rules follow each exporter's resolved endpoint. In the connectivity chart a `dataPlaneEnv` entry now wins over `global.observability.traces.otlp` (it used to lose), and `make verify-otlp-global` asserts the derivation and the egress rules.
